description:
Industry Upgrades Continued

Industry Upgrades by stardorn is one of the best economy mods for Transport Fever 3. Your industries earn experience, and you spend it on throughput, storage, efficiency, booster, environmental filter and worker boost upgrades, or you pay with deliveries of cargo. All the ideas and almost all of the code are the original author's work. This mod continues it with fixes and a few new options.

How to switch

  1. Deactivate the original Industry Upgrades in your savegame, and activate this mod instead. Never run both together: they upgrade the same industries.
  2. Your savegame keeps the upgrade levels already built. Points, EXP, levels still waiting for their rebuild and open delivery orders start fresh, and you choose the mod settings again.

Fixes

  • Fixed: upgrades stuck at "Upgrading to level X in a few seconds". The game can refuse to rebuild an industry, most often because of a sharp bend where its access road meets your roads. The mod now notices this, shows a Rebuild refused section with the cause and what to do, and retries every month. In EXP mode a button returns the points of the waiting levels.
  • EXP and upkeep should no longer run several times per month at a slow calendar speed. They now run once per calendar month at every calendar speed.
  • Efficiency upgrades should no longer make huge production batches (77 logs instead of 4 per cycle). A cycle now uses at most 5 times the game's amounts.

New options and texts

  • Up to 40 workers: while Workers needed per level is on, industries with worker boost levels count up to 40 workers (the game counts 20), and their workplaces stop at 80. For this the mod replaces the game's worker script, which can conflict with other mods that change workers. With Workers needed per level Off, nothing is replaced.
  • Partial worker boost: while Workers needed per level is on, the boost grows with the workers: 15 of 40 workers give 15/40 of the boost. The worker row in the industry window shows the boost now, with Max. and the full boost under it.
  • The calculation of the workers needed shows on the worker boost card, in red when it is above 20.
  • Number of worker boost levels: 5 or 10.
  • Tidier settings: every setting name starts with its group (Throughput, Storage, Efficiency, Booster, Environmental filter, Worker boost, Upkeep, EXP points, Deliveries), and Upgrade costs sits below Upkeep.
  • Clearer texts: the booster card says when its inputs were built under another booster demand setting, and the help says that a changed setting reaches built levels at the next upgrade. All texts are in 9 languages.

Credits

  • stardorn made Industry Upgrades. Everything good in this mod starts there.
  • Claude AI (Anthropic) is the development assistant of this continuation (with my own control and validation).

The source code can be found here, PRs are welcome: kergekacsa/tf3_industry_upgrades_continued on GitHub

If you find this mod useful, please rate the original Industry Upgrades too.
name: Industry Upgrades Continued
summary: The Industry Upgrades mod, continued: bug fixes, a 40-worker limit and a partial worker boost.
